name: Avoiding Design Mistakes That Drive Up Los Angeles Bathroom Remodel Costs

mainEntity.name: What are the main design mistakes that cause cost overruns on Los Angeles bathroom remodels, and how can I avoid them?
mainEntity.text: What are the main design mistakes that cause cost overruns on Los Angeles bathroom remodels, and how can I avoid them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bathroom remodels often run over budget not because of obvious upgrades, but due to early design missteps. One major mistake is **changing plumbing locations midstream**—for example, moving a shower or toilet after rough plumbing is installed or discovering that a desired trench drain conflicts with existing joists or slab conditions. These changes trigger extra demolition, framing, and inspections. Another issue is selecting tile, fixtures, and glass after construction begins. If sizes and lead times are not known, installers may frame or rough-in incorrectly, then have to redo work when actual products arrive. Custom niches, shower benches, or linear drains should be fully designed and dimensioned in advance. Homeowners also underestimate the importance of **ventilation and waterproofing**. Properly sloped shower pans, continuous waterproofing membranes, and appropriately sized, ducted exhaust fans are essential. Skimping here can lead to moisture problems and later repairs. To avoid overruns, finalize a **detailed plan set** and product list before demolition. Confirm structural constraints, valve locations, tile layouts, and glass configurations up front. Ask your contractor to flag any selections that could affect framing, plumbing, or electrical before work starts, and build a small contingency into your budget for hidden conditions.
acceptedAnswer.description: Common mistakes include moving plumbing fixtures without understanding structural or slab limits, choosing tile or fixtures after rough-in, and underestimating ventilation and waterproofing needs. Lock in a detailed layout and product selections before work starts to minimize change orders and delays.
